units.text: This chapter rewards reaching. You are paid back for every offer you take up and put to use straight away.
This chapter spreads you thin. You hold your ground when your own strength comes first and the chase comes second.
Two things on the go|one slow project
One piece of work finished|two half started
Doing up the house together|each doing their own
Turning up to help|paying someone to
A task a size too big|a book on the subject
Getting better at what you have|adding something new
A day on your feet|a morning in bed
A slow afternoon|a list that keeps growing
New plans as a pair|the usual weekend
An evening with no plans|another shared project
A problem you can fix by hand|an idea on paper
One decision at a time|ten open questions
Friends who do business|friends who just chat
A walk with a friend|a networking event
Money from two places|more from one
Clearing a debt|signing for a new one
This chapter tops up a strength your chart has always run short of. You get the most from it among equals, in teams and contests where you can measure yourself.
This chapter fills you with more of your own strength than you can store. You do best when you spend it, on hard work and on people who need what you know.
Work you own outright|work someone else signs off
The work itself|who gets the credit
Saying what you need|fitting round others
Letting a point drop|winning every one
Doing it yourself|waiting for help
Beating your own mark|beating someone else's
Effort you can keep up|one big burst
Sweating it off|bottling it up
Holding your own view|agreeing to please
Letting the other choose|always choosing first
Your own conclusions|what everyone else thinks
Checking with someone you trust|going with your gut
Friends who match your pace|friends who carry you
Cheering others on|keeping score
Paying your own way|someone else picking up the bill
Separate savings|a kitty with friends
This chapter opens an outlet your chart has long been short of. You gain most when you finish what you start and let other people see it.
This chapter loosens your tongue and your appetite more than your chart can use. You keep your standing when you wait before you answer and speak once.
Showing your work|keeping it in a drawer
Saying it once|saying it twice
Making a mess together|keeping it spotless
Hearing them out|having your say
A public showing|private practice
Getting it right|getting it seen
A dance class|a gym routine
Plain meals|rich food
Saying how you feel|hoping it shows
A quiet evening in|a big night out
Making something|studying how it is made
One notebook filled|five begun
Hosting a dinner|waiting for an invite
Listening first|the last word
Selling what you make|a fixed wage
Waiting a week before buying|buying on the spot
This chapter feeds you with learning, help and rest. You draw the most from it through slow study and the people who back you.
This chapter wraps you in more thought and shelter than you can use. You are lighter on days when your hands are busy and one question gets settled.
Being shown the ropes|a grander title
Making a start|waiting until you are ready
A quiet evening at home|a full house
Cooking for someone|being cooked for
Lessons from someone who knows|guesswork on your own
One skill used daily|three half-learned
A day off when you need it|pushing on through
Getting outside|another day indoors
Letting yourself be looked after|doing it all yourself
A shared task|a long talk about the two of you
A long book|a quick scroll
A choice made today|another week of weighing
A friend who listens|a crowd that cheers
Setting a date to meet|meaning to get in touch
A course that pays off later|quick cash now
Moving the money|reading about where to move it
This chapter gives your strength the shape it has lacked. Clear roles and firm deadlines bring out your best, and you rise when someone holds you to a standard.
This chapter bears down on you from outside. You carry it best with something of your own it cannot reach, a friend, a slower pace or a quiet place.
Keeping a role|starting a new one
Work you set yourself|orders from above
Your word at home|winning a point
Letting the dishes wait|a rota for everything
A title to earn|a path of your own
Learning for the fun of it|being marked on it
A set training plan|exercise when you like
A day with no alarm|a packed schedule
A clear commitment|keeping it casual
Easy evenings|rules about who does what
A proper course|dabbling
Thinking for yourself|thinking what is expected
A club with a job to do|friends for laughs
Friends with no agenda|contacts from work
Money on the same day each month|money when it comes
A budget you set|bills set for you
